hook.line: Every café has a *what if* table: the regulars who say they should have bought the building years ago. English says *I wish I had known*. Spanish has a form built for exactly that, and you already own both halves of it.

examples.en: I wish you had come. (to a friend)
I wish we had arrived earlier.
I wish I hadn't said anything.

examples.es: No creí que hubieran vendido el edificio.
examples.en: I didn't think they had sold the building.

rule:
You know *había* + participle for what had already happened: *había sabido*. For a wish about the past, swap *había* for *hubiera*:
*hubiera*, *hubieras*, *hubiera*, *hubiéramos*, *hubieran*

Then add the participle, which never changes: *hubiera sabido*, *hubieras venido*, *hubiéramos llegado*.

So *Ojalá viniera* wishes for something now (*I wish she were coming*), while *Ojalá hubiera venido* looks back (*I wish she had come*). The past is closed, so the wish can only be a wish.

The same form follows *no creí que* and other past doubts: *No creí que hubieran vendido*. English just says *had*; Spanish makes you pick the *hubiera* form.
smallPrint: Teachers call this the pluperfect subjunctive (*pluscuamperfecto de subjuntivo*). You will also see *hubiese* in books. It means the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *supiera* or *hubiera sabido* and type the whole sentence: *Ojalá lo ___.* (I wish I had known it back then.)
yourTurn.why: Looking back at the past, you need *hubiera* plus the participle.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *hubieras* or *hubiéramos* and type the whole sentence: *Ojalá ___ venido.* (I wish you had come. To a friend.)
yourTurn.why: *Hubieras* is the *tú* form, and the participle stays *venido*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I wish we had arrived earlier.
yourTurn.why: *Hubiéramos* carries the *we*, with an accent on the vowel before *ramos*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I wish Vale had stayed.
yourTurn.why: *Se hubiera quedado*: the *se* stays in front of the helper.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Ojalá lo hubiera dicho.* (I wish I had said it. Now: I wish I hadn't said it.)
yourTurn.why: *No* goes in front of everything, including *lo*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about they: *Ojalá hubiera llegado antes.*
yourTurn.why: *Hubieran* is the form for *they*; the participle doesn't change.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: I didn't think they had sold the building.
yourTurn.answer: No creí que hubieran vendido el edificio.
yourTurn.why: After a past doubt, use *hubieran* plus the participle.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Había* states a fact; a wish about the past needs *hubiera*.
The verb after *hubiera* is the participle: *venido*.
After *hubiéramos* comes the participle, not the infinitive.

personal: Think of something you'd do differently. Say it: *Ojalá hubiera...* or *Ojalá no hubiera...*.
